messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated KV cache evictions (x10 baseline) and a spike in batch scheduler tail latency across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Failure rate up ~3.2% for text-gen endpoints. Automated paging created.

maya-oncall: seeing the alert, joining. paging: P0? any suspected deploys in last 10m?

ravi: pushed a batch-config tweak ~8m ago (optimize/continuous-batching v1.4.2) to reduce token-wait. logs show KV cache size jumped from 20GB -> 180GB as prefixes weren't being reused, eviction storm started. dropping into paging. sample logs: ```WARN kv_cache: evicting 12000 entries in 30s
WARN batch_sched: long_waiters=42, short_waiters=120, avg_batch_tokens=980```

sre-ops: confirmed. schedule: mixed long/short requests started starving small requests. continuous-batching seems to aggressively aggregate and cause oversized batches which blow the KV cache and push paging.

maya-oncall: immediate mitigation plan? customer impact assessment please (CS).

customer-success: affected tenants: 3 high-throughput producers showing >5% error rate, several enterprise customers reported timeouts. Notified a few clients via status page; CS is standing by.

sre-ops: mitigation steps I'm proposing (in order):
1) flip feature flag: disable continuous-batching globally (quick revert).
2) reduce max_batch_time_ms from 50 -> 10 for now.
3) temporarily lower per-worker kv_cache_max_bytes to force aggressive backpressure (avoid node-level OOMs).
4) apply scheduler cap: per-pod concurrent_batch_slots=4 to avoid long-request monopolization.

maya-oncall: execute 1 and 2 now. li-chen, can you do the flag flip? ravi, can you push a hotpatch for scheduler cap?

li-chen: flipping flag now. curl to FF service: ```curl -X POST https://ff.redwood.internal/api/toggle -d '{"feature":"continuous_batching","enabled":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'``` -> response 200. Propagating to edge ~15s.

li-chen: changed max_batch_time_ms config via config service: ```PATCH /config/batching {"max_batch_time_ms":10}``` -> reload on config daemon sent to nodes.

ravi: scheduler hotfix PR submitted w/ cap slot change + tests. rolling to canary (1/10) now: ```kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/batch-scheduler-canary```

dev-runtime: added temporary guard in scheduler: if request_size_tokens > 512 then route to long-req pool; also added fairness token bucket to limit short-request starvation. Deploying to canary.

sre-ops: monitoring metrics: eviction rate down 60% within 45s of flag flip, page writes trending back to normal. tail latency p99 for small requests starting to recover.

customer-success: CS update: error rate dropping for affected tenants, sending follow-up. customers want root cause + ETA for full restore.

maya-oncall: good. start incident timeline and collect logs for postmortem. Assigning tasks:
- ravi: collect perf traces, payload samples, and exact commit that introduced regression.
- li-chen: write debuggable revert playbook and confirm flag propagation across regions.
- dev-runtime: follow-up hotfix to scheduler to enforce per-tenant fairness (long-term).
- jules: prepare status update for customers and internal comms.

incident-bot: Escalation: Pager duty notified to SRE rotation (level 2).

li-chen: verified global propagation. all regions show feature disabled.

ravi: PR merged, scheduler cap rolled to 50% of nodes; monitoring shows no more oversized batches. posted short log snippet: ```INFO batch_sched: batch_slots=4 enforced, avg_tokens_per_batch=210```

maya-oncall: switching to mitigation-confirmed state. No current customer-facing incidents open; CS keep monitoring for 1 hour.

ajay: taking handoff for 0600 UTC rotation. I'll drive the postmortem tomorrow and ensure a rollback plan for any related configs. ack :handshake: 

maya-oncall: thanks ajay. next steps: create postmortem ticket, label as perf-regression + kv-eviction, link PRs and flag timeline. leaving channel for async follow-up.

jules: posting incident summary to #incidents-postmortems later today.

maya-oncall: all, please upload traces and any unusual request samples to the incident doc. closing live thread, moving to postmortem lane. :white_check_mark:
